records.literal_gloss: And it was, when he finished speaking to Saul, and [the] soul of Jonathan was bound to [the] soul of David, and loved him Jonathan as his [own] soul.

en.L: And it happened, when he had finished speaking to Saul, that the soul of Jonathan was bound to the soul of David, and Jonathan loved him as his own soul.
en.B: When David had finished speaking with Saul, Jonathan's life became bound up with David's life, and Jonathan loved him as he loved himself.
en.R: David finished talking with Saul. Then Saul's son Jonathan felt closely joined to David. He loved David as much as he loved himself.

es.L: Y sucedió que, cuando terminó de hablar con Saúl, el alma de Jonatán quedó ligada al alma de David, y lo amó Jonatán como a su propia alma.
es.B: Cuando David terminó de hablar con Saúl, la vida de Jonatán quedó unida a la vida de David, y Jonatán lo amó como se amaba a sí mismo.
es.R: David terminó de hablar con Saúl. Entonces Jonatán, el hijo de Saúl, se sintió muy unido a David. Lo quería tanto como se quería a sí mismo.

fr.L: Et il arriva, quand il eut fini de parler à Saül, que l’âme de Jonathan s’attacha à l’âme de David, et Jonathan l’aima comme sa propre âme.
fr.B: Quand David eut fini de parler avec Saül, la vie de Jonathan se trouva liée à celle de David, et Jonathan l’aima comme lui-même.
fr.R: David a fini de parler avec Saül. Alors Jonathan, le fils de Saül, s’est senti très proche de David. Il l’aimait autant qu’il s’aimait lui-même.

sw.L: Ikawa alipokwisha kusema na Sauli, nafsi ya Yonathani ikafungamana na nafsi ya Daudi, naye Yonathani akampenda kama nafsi yake mwenyewe.
sw.B: Daudi alipomaliza kuzungumza na Sauli, maisha ya Yonathani yakafungamana na maisha ya Daudi, naye Yonathani akampenda kama alivyojipenda mwenyewe.
sw.R: Daudi akamaliza kuzungumza na Sauli. Kisha Yonathani, mwana wa Sauli, akajisikia ameungana sana na Daudi. Akampenda Daudi kama alivyojipenda mwenyewe.

vi.L: Khi Đa-vít đã nói xong với Sau-lơ, linh hồn Giô-na-than gắn bó với linh hồn Đa-vít, và Giô-na-than yêu Đa-vít như chính linh hồn mình.
vi.B: Khi Đa-vít nói chuyện với Sau-lơ xong, lòng Giô-na-than gắn bó với lòng Đa-vít, và Giô-na-than yêu Đa-vít như yêu chính mình.
vi.R: Đa-vít nói chuyện với Sau-lơ xong. Bấy giờ Giô-na-than, con trai Sau-lơ, cảm thấy rất gắn bó với Đa-vít. Giô-na-than yêu Đa-vít như yêu chính mình.

ko.L: 그리고 그가 사울에게 말하기를 마쳤을 때, 요나단의 영혼이 다윗의 영혼에 묶였다. 그리고 요나단은 그를 자기 영혼처럼 사랑했다.
ko.B: 다윗이 사울과 이야기를 마쳤을 때, 요나단의 마음이 다윗의 마음과 하나로 묶였다. 요나단은 다윗을 자기 자신처럼 사랑했다.
ko.R: 다윗이 사울과 이야기를 마쳤다. 그때 사울의 아들 요나단은 다윗에게 마음이 깊이 끌렸다. 요나단은 다윗을 자기 자신만큼 사랑했다.

pt.L: E aconteceu que, quando ele acabou de falar com Saul, a alma de Jônatas se ligou à alma de Davi, e Jônatas amou-o como à sua própria alma.
pt.B: Quando Davi terminou de falar com Saul, a vida de Jônatas ficou ligada à vida de Davi, e Jônatas amou-o como a si mesmo.
pt.R: Davi terminou de falar com Saul. Então Jônatas, o filho de Saul, sentiu-se muito unido a Davi. Ele amava Davi tanto quanto amava a si mesmo.

am.L: እንዲህም ሆነ፤ ከሳኦል ጋር ተናግሮ በፈጸመ ጊዜ የዮናታን ነፍስ ከዳዊት ነፍስ ጋር ተቆራኘች፤ ዮናታንም እንደ ገዛ ነፍሱ ወደደው።
am.B: ዳዊት ከሳኦል ጋር ተነጋግሮ ሲጨርስ የዮናታን ነፍስ ከዳዊት ነፍስ ጋር ተሳሰረች፤ ዮናታንም ራሱን እንደሚወድ ዳዊትን ወደደው።
am.R: ዳዊት ከሳኦል ጋር መነጋገሩን ጨረሰ። ከዚያም የሳኦል ልጅ ዮናታን በልቡ ከዳዊት ጋር በጥብቅ ተቆራኘ። ራሱን የሚወደውን ያህል ዳዊትን ወደደው።

decisions.choice: the soul of Jonathan was bound to the soul of David: Jonathan was deeply attached to David
decisions.reason: The word often rendered "soul" means a person's life and inner self. The same picture of one life bound to another is used of Jacob and Benjamin in Genesis 44:30. It describes a close and lasting attachment.

decisions.choice: loved him as his own soul: loved him as he loved himself
decisions.reason: "As his own soul" means "as himself" (compare Deuteronomy 13:7). The words are repeated in verse 3 and 20:17. Love in this book is also the word for loyalty given to a leader: all Israel and Judah "loved" David (verse 16), and Saul's servants "love" him (verse 22). Jonathan's love is personal, and it is also the loyalty of a king's son to the man who will be king (23:17).

decisions.choice: the Hebrew text includes 17:55-18:5 and the other passages of this chapter
alternatives: the shorter Greek text without these verses
decisions.reason: The main early Greek manuscript (Codex Vaticanus) has a shorter form of chapters 17 and 18. Among other passages it lacks 17:55-18:5, 18:10-11, 18:17-19 and 18:29b-30. Some think that this shorter form is older and that the Hebrew text joins two accounts of how David came to Saul's court; others think the Greek shortened the story to smooth over its repetitions. The Hebrew text is translated here in full. Reviewers should check the evidence before this sentence is marked reviewed.

decisions.choice: Jonathan's life became bound up with David's life (Balanced); felt closely joined to David (Readable)
decisions.reason: "Soul" in modern speech suggests the spiritual part of a person, while the Hebrew word means the whole self and life. Readable adds that Jonathan is Saul's son, which the reader learned in chapters 13 and 14.

decisions.choice: l'âme (L); la vie (B); s'est senti très proche (R)
decisions.reason: As the English (r-en-1): "âme" in modern French suggests the spiritual part of a person, while the Hebrew word means the whole living self (m1); Literal keeps the image, Balanced says "la vie", Readable the feeling.

decisions.choice: el alma de Jonatán ... al alma de David (L); la vida de Jonatán ... a la vida de David (B)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew nefesh is the whole self (m1). Literal keeps “alma”; Balanced says “vida”, as the English “life” (r-en-1); Readable says how Jonathan felt.

decisions.choice: "nafsi" (L); "maisha" (B); the person himself (R)
decisions.reason: As the Psalms note: *nefesh* is "nafsi" at Literal. Balanced says "maisha" (life) and Readable speaks of the two men themselves, as the English does (m1).

decisions.choice: "linh hồn" (L); "lòng" (B)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps *nefesh* as "linh hồn" (Psalms terms note); Balanced uses "lòng", the Vietnamese seat of attachment, for a man's whole self bound to another (m1).

decisions.choice: "마음" (heart) for *nefesh* at Balanced; "영혼" at Literal
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "영혼", the word the terms of this translation set for *nefesh* at Literal; Balanced says what is bound together, Jonathan's inner self to David's (meaning decision m1), with the ordinary Korean word for it.

decisions.choice: amou-o como à sua própria alma (L); amou-o como a si mesmo (B); tanto quanto amava a si mesmo (R)
alternatives: o amou como à sua alma (B)
decisions.reason: "As his own soul" means "as himself" (m2), so Balanced says "como a si mesmo", the wording kept again in verse 3 and 20:17; Literal keeps "alma", the word of the first half of the verse, as the English Literal keeps "soul". "Jônatas" is the usual Brazilian form of the name, for the whole book.

decisions.choice: No deity_pronoun spans in the Amharic of 1 Samuel 18.
decisions.reason: The Ethiopic script has no capital letters, so the setting that capitalises pronouns for God has nothing to change in Amharic; pronouns for God are written plainly.

decisions.choice: "ነፍስ" (soul, life, self) for both souls, with "ተቆራኘች" (L) / "ተሳሰረች" (B)
decisions.reason: Amharic "ነፍስ" means both a person's life and inner self, as the Hebrew word does, so Balanced can keep the picture that English renders as "life"; Readable says plainly that Jonathan was bound to David "in his heart" ("በልቡ").

source.text: וַיִּקָּחֵ֥הוּ שָׁא֖וּל בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֑וּא וְלֹ֣א נְתָנ֔וֹ לָשׁ֖וּב בֵּ֥ית אָבִֽיו׃

records.literal_gloss: And took him Saul on the day the that, and not did he let him return [to the] house of his father.

en.L: And Saul took him on that day and did not let him return to his father's house.
en.B: From that day on Saul kept David with him and would not let him go back to his father's house.
en.R: From that day on, Saul kept David at his court. He did not let him go back home to his father's family.

es.L: Y lo tomó Saúl aquel día, y no lo dejó volver a la casa de su padre.
es.B: Desde aquel día Saúl retuvo a David consigo y no lo dejó volver a la casa de su padre.
es.R: Desde aquel día, Saúl tuvo a David en su corte. No lo dejó volver a casa con la familia de su padre.

fr.L: Et Saül le prit ce jour-là, et il ne le laissa pas retourner à la maison de son père.
fr.B: À partir de ce jour, Saül garda David auprès de lui et ne le laissa plus retourner dans la maison de son père.
fr.R: À partir de ce jour-là, Saül a gardé David à sa cour. Il ne l’a plus laissé rentrer chez lui, dans la famille de son père.

sw.L: Sauli akamchukua siku ile, wala hakumwacha arudi nyumbani kwa baba yake.
sw.B: Tangu siku ile Sauli akamweka Daudi pamoja naye, wala hakumruhusu arudi nyumbani kwa baba yake.
sw.R: Tangu siku ile, Sauli akamweka Daudi katika jumba lake la kifalme. Hakumruhusu arudi nyumbani kwa jamaa ya baba yake.

vi.L: Ngày hôm đó Sau-lơ giữ Đa-vít lại và không để ông trở về nhà cha mình.
vi.B: Từ hôm đó, Sau-lơ giữ Đa-vít ở lại với mình và không cho ông trở về nhà cha nữa.
vi.R: Từ hôm đó, Sau-lơ giữ Đa-vít ở lại trong cung. Vua không cho ông trở về nhà với gia đình cha mình nữa.

ko.L: 그리고 사울이 그날 그를 데려가서 그의 아버지의 집으로 돌아가지 못하게 했다.
ko.B: 그날부터 사울은 다윗을 곁에 두고, 그가 아버지의 집으로 돌아가지 못하게 했다.
ko.R: 그날부터 사울은 다윗을 자기 궁에 머물게 했다. 다윗이 아버지의 집으로 돌아가지 못하게 했다.

pt.L: E Saul o tomou naquele dia e não o deixou voltar para a casa do seu pai.
pt.B: Daquele dia em diante, Saul manteve Davi consigo e não o deixou voltar para a casa do pai.
pt.R: Daquele dia em diante, Saul manteve Davi na sua corte. Não o deixou voltar para casa, para a família do pai.

am.L: ሳኦልም በዚያ ቀን ወሰደው፤ ወደ አባቱም ቤት እንዲመለስ አልፈቀደለትም።
am.B: ከዚያን ቀን ጀምሮ ሳኦል ዳዊትን ከእርሱ ጋር አስቀረው፤ ወደ አባቱ ቤት እንዲመለስም አልፈቀደለትም።
am.R: ከዚያን ቀን ጀምሮ ሳኦል ዳዊትን በቤተ መንግሥቱ አስቀመጠው። ወደ አባቱ ቤተሰብ እንዲመለስ አልፈቀደለትም።

decisions.choice: Saul took him: David now served at the king's court
decisions.reason: Samuel had warned that a king would take Israel's sons into his service (8:11). David had gone back and forth between Saul and his father's flocks (17:15); from now on he stays with Saul.

decisions.choice: From that day on ... kept David with him
decisions.reason: "Took him" means Saul took David into his service. Balanced and Readable say that he kept him, and Readable names the court.

source.text: וַיִּכְרֹ֧ת יְהוֹנָתָ֛ן וְדָוִ֖ד בְּרִ֑ית בְּאַהֲבָת֥וֹ אֹת֖וֹ כְּנַפְשֽׁוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: And made Jonathan and David a covenant, because he loved him as his [own] soul.

en.L: And Jonathan and David made a covenant, because he loved him as his own soul.
en.B: Jonathan made a covenant with David, because he loved him as he loved himself.
en.R: Jonathan made a covenant with David, a solemn promise to be loyal to each other, because he loved him as much as he loved himself.

es.L: E hicieron Jonatán y David un pacto, porque lo amaba como a su propia alma.
es.B: Jonatán hizo un pacto con David, porque lo amaba como se amaba a sí mismo.
es.R: Jonatán hizo un pacto con David, una promesa solemne de ser leales el uno al otro, porque lo quería tanto como se quería a sí mismo.

fr.L: Et Jonathan et David conclurent une alliance, parce qu’il l’aimait comme sa propre âme.
fr.B: Jonathan conclut une alliance avec David, parce qu’il l’aimait comme lui-même.
fr.R: Jonathan a fait une alliance avec David : ils se sont promis solennellement d’être fidèles l’un à l’autre. Jonathan aimait David autant qu’il s’aimait lui-même.

sw.L: Yonathani na Daudi wakafanya agano, kwa sababu alimpenda kama nafsi yake mwenyewe.
sw.B: Yonathani akafanya agano na Daudi, kwa sababu alimpenda kama alivyojipenda mwenyewe.
sw.R: Yonathani akafanya agano na Daudi, yaani ahadi nzito ya kuwa waaminifu kila mmoja kwa mwenzake, kwa sababu alimpenda kama alivyojipenda mwenyewe.

vi.L: Giô-na-than và Đa-vít lập giao ước, vì Giô-na-than yêu Đa-vít như chính linh hồn mình.
vi.B: Giô-na-than lập giao ước với Đa-vít, vì Giô-na-than yêu Đa-vít như yêu chính mình.
vi.R: Giô-na-than lập giao ước với Đa-vít, tức là một lời hứa long trọng sẽ trung thành với nhau, vì Giô-na-than yêu Đa-vít như yêu chính mình.

ko.L: 그리고 요나단과 다윗이 언약을 맺었다. 그가 그를 자기 영혼처럼 사랑했기 때문이다.
ko.B: 요나단은 다윗을 자기 자신처럼 사랑했으므로 다윗과 언약을 맺었다.
ko.R: 요나단은 다윗을 자기 자신만큼 사랑했다. 그래서 요나단은 다윗과 언약을 맺었다. 그것은 서로에게 끝까지 충실하겠다는 엄숙한 약속이었다.

pt.L: E Jônatas e Davi fizeram uma aliança, porque ele o amava como à sua própria alma.
pt.B: Jônatas fez uma aliança com Davi, porque o amava como a si mesmo.
pt.R: Jônatas fez uma aliança com Davi, uma promessa solene de serem leais um ao outro, porque o amava tanto quanto amava a si mesmo.

am.L: ዮናታንና ዳዊትም ቃል ኪዳን አደረጉ፤ እንደ ገዛ ነፍሱ ወድዶታልና።
am.B: ዮናታን ራሱን እንደሚወድ ዳዊትን ይወደው ስለ ነበር ከእርሱ ጋር ቃል ኪዳን አደረገ።
am.R: ዮናታን ራሱን የሚወደውን ያህል ዳዊትን ይወደው ስለ ነበር ከእርሱ ጋር ቃል ኪዳን አደረገ፤ ይህም አንዳቸው ለሌላው ታማኝ ለመሆን የገቡት ጽኑ ቃል ነበር።

decisions.choice: made a covenant: a binding agreement of loyalty, sworn before God
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says a covenant was "cut". A covenant bound two parties with an oath, often in Yahweh's name (20:8, 42). This covenant is recalled in 20:8-17 and 23:18, and David keeps it after Jonathan's death for the sake of Jonathan's son (2 Samuel 9:1-7; 21:7).

decisions.choice: because he loved him: Jonathan loved David
decisions.reason: The pronouns are unclear on their own, but verse 1 and the next verse show that Jonathan is the one who loves and who takes the lead.

decisions.choice: a covenant, a solemn promise to be loyal to each other
decisions.reason: Readable keeps the word "covenant" and explains it once for new readers.

decisions.choice: une alliance
decisions.reason: As the Samuel terms note sets: the covenant between David and Jonathan is "alliance" at every level, the word for God's covenant too; Readable explains it once, as the English does (r-en-1).

decisions.choice: pacto
decisions.reason: As the Samuel terms note sets for the covenant between David and Jonathan, the same word as God's covenant in the Pentateuch; Readable explains it, as the English does (r-en-1). Recorded once for this block.

decisions.choice: "giao ước" at every level
decisions.reason: The Samuel terms note's word for the covenant between David and Jonathan, the same word as God's covenant; Readable explains it as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: after this covenant David speaks to Jonathan in the polite informal style (해요체), Jonathan to David in the plain style (해라체)
decisions.reason: As the terms of this translation set for Korean: David speaks 합쇼체 to the king's son before their covenant and 해요체 after it; Jonathan, the king's son, speaks 해라체. "언약" is the word for the covenant between them.

source.text: וַיִּתְפַּשֵּׁ֣ט יְהוֹנָתָ֗ן אֶֽת־הַמְּעִיל֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר עָלָ֔יו וַֽיִּתְּנֵ֖הוּ לְדָוִ֑ד וּמַדָּ֕יו וְעַד־חַרְבּ֥וֹ וְעַד־קַשְׁתּ֖וֹ וְעַד־חֲגֹרֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: And stripped himself Jonathan [of] the robe that [was] on him and gave it to David, and his garments, and even his sword and even his bow and even his belt.

en.L: And Jonathan stripped himself of the robe that [was] on him and gave it to David, and his garments, even his sword and his bow and his belt.
en.B: Jonathan stripped off the robe he had on and handed it to David, together with his battle clothing, and even his sword, his bow and his belt.
en.R: Jonathan took off the robe he had on and gave it to David. He also gave him his soldier's clothes, and even his sword, his bow and his belt.

es.L: Y se quitó Jonatán el manto que [llevaba] sobre sí y se lo dio a David, y sus ropas, y hasta su espada, su arco y su cinturón.
es.B: Jonatán se quitó el manto que llevaba puesto y se lo dio a David, junto con su ropa de combate, y hasta su espada, su arco y su cinturón.
es.R: Jonatán se quitó el manto que tenía puesto y se lo dio a David. También le dio su ropa de soldado, y hasta su espada, su arco y su cinturón.

fr.L: Et Jonathan se dépouilla du manteau qui [était] sur lui et le donna à David, ainsi que ses vêtements, et même son épée, et même son arc, et même sa ceinture.
fr.B: Jonathan retira le manteau qu’il portait et le donna à David, avec sa tenue de combat, et même son épée, son arc et sa ceinture.
fr.R: Jonathan a enlevé le manteau qu’il portait et il l’a donné à David. Il lui a aussi donné ses vêtements de soldat, et même son épée, son arc et sa ceinture.

sw.L: Yonathani akalivua joho lililokuwa juu yake, akampa Daudi, pamoja na mavazi yake, hata upanga wake, na upinde wake, na mshipi wake.
sw.B: Yonathani akalivua joho alilokuwa amevaa, akampa Daudi, pamoja na mavazi yake ya vita, hata upanga wake, upinde wake na mshipi wake.
sw.R: Yonathani akavua joho alilokuwa amevaa, akampa Daudi. Akampa pia mavazi yake ya kiaskari, hata upanga wake, upinde wake na mshipi wake.

vi.L: Giô-na-than cởi chiếc áo choàng đang mặc trên mình và trao cho Đa-vít, cùng với y phục của mình, cả gươm, cung và đai lưng.
vi.B: Giô-na-than cởi chiếc áo choàng mình đang mặc trao cho Đa-vít, cùng với bộ chiến bào, và cả gươm, cung và đai lưng của mình nữa.
vi.R: Giô-na-than cởi chiếc áo choàng mình đang mặc và trao cho Đa-vít. Anh cũng trao cho Đa-vít bộ quân phục, và cả gươm, cung và thắt lưng của mình.

ko.L: 그리고 요나단이 자기가 입고 있던 겉옷을 벗어 다윗에게 주고, 자기 군복과 칼과 활과 띠까지 주었다.
ko.B: 요나단은 자기가 입고 있던 겉옷을 벗어 다윗에게 주었다. 자기 군복과 칼과 활과 허리띠까지 주었다.
ko.R: 요나단은 자기가 입고 있던 겉옷을 벗어 다윗에게 주었다. 자기가 입던 군복도 주고, 칼과 활과 허리띠까지 다윗에게 주었다.

pt.L: E Jônatas despiu o manto que [estava] sobre ele e o deu a Davi, e as suas roupas, até a sua espada, e o seu arco, e o seu cinto.
pt.B: Jônatas tirou o manto que vestia e o deu a Davi, junto com a sua roupa de guerra, e até a sua espada, o seu arco e o seu cinto.
pt.R: Jônatas tirou o manto que estava usando e o deu a Davi. Deu-lhe também a sua roupa de soldado, e até a sua espada, o seu arco e o seu cinto.

am.L: ዮናታንም በላዩ የነበረውን መጎናጸፊያ አውልቆ ለዳዊት ሰጠው፤ ልብሱንም፣ ሰይፉንም፣ ቀስቱንም፣ ቀበቶውንም ጭምር [ሰጠው]።
am.B: ዮናታን የለበሰውን መጎናጸፊያ አውልቆ ለዳዊት ሰጠው፤ የጦር ልብሱንም፣ ሰይፉን፣ ቀስቱንና ቀበቶውን ሳይቀር ሰጠው።
am.R: ዮናታን የለበሰውን ካባ አውልቆ ለዳዊት ሰጠው። የወታደር ልብሱንም ሰጠው፤ ሰይፉን፣ ቀስቱንና ቀበቶውን እንኳ ሰጠው።

decisions.choice: the robe and the weapons: the gift of a king's son
decisions.reason: The robe was a fine outer garment worn by people of rank (2:19; 15:27; 24:5). Jonathan, the heir to Saul's throne, gives David his own robe and his weapons. The gift seals the covenant, and it points ahead to Jonathan's words in 23:17: "you will be king over Israel, and I will be second to you."

decisions.choice: his garments: his tunic or battle dress
decisions.reason: The word means a garment, here worn with weapons; it is used of Saul's battle clothing in 17:38-39, which David could not wear. Its exact form is not known.

decisions.choice: his sword and his bow: Jonathan's own weapons
decisions.reason: In 13:22 only Saul and Jonathan had swords in Israel. David had refused Saul's armor (17:38-39); Jonathan's gift is freely given and freely taken. Jonathan was known for his bow (20:20, 36; 2 Samuel 1:22).

decisions.choice: battle clothing (Balanced); soldier's clothes (Readable)
decisions.reason: The word goes with weapons here, so Balanced and Readable say what kind of clothing it was.

decisions.choice: robe: "መጎናጸፊያ" (L, B), "ካባ" (R)
decisions.reason: "መጎናጸፊያ" is the word settled in Exodus for the robe (me'il); the same garment returns in 24:4-5, where it is cut. Readable uses the everyday word for a cloak.

source.text: וַיֵּצֵ֨א דָוִ֜ד בְּכֹל֩ אֲשֶׁ֨ר יִשְׁלָחֶ֤נּוּ שָׁאוּל֙ יַשְׂכִּ֔יל וַיְשִׂמֵ֣הוּ שָׁא֔וּל עַ֖ל אַנְשֵׁ֣י הַמִּלְחָמָ֑ה וַיִּיטַב֙ בְּעֵינֵ֣י כָל־הָעָ֔ם וְגַ֕ם בְּעֵינֵ֖י עַבְדֵ֥י שָׁאֽוּל׃פ

records.literal_gloss: And went out David; in all that sent him Saul he succeeded, and set him Saul over the men of the war; and it was good in [the] eyes of all the people and also in [the] eyes of [the] servants of Saul.

en.L: And David went out; wherever Saul sent him, he succeeded, and Saul set him over the men of war. And it was good in the eyes of all the people and also in the eyes of Saul's servants.
en.B: David went out wherever Saul sent him, and he succeeded every time, so Saul put him in charge of the fighting men. This pleased all the people, and Saul's officials too.
en.R: Saul sent David out on many missions, and every time David did well. So Saul made him a leader over the soldiers. All the people were glad about this, and so were Saul's officials.

es.L: Y salía David; a dondequiera que lo enviaba Saúl, tenía éxito, y lo puso Saúl sobre los hombres de guerra. Y pareció bien a los ojos de todo el pueblo, y también a los ojos de los siervos de Saúl.
es.B: David salía a dondequiera que Saúl lo enviaba, y siempre tenía éxito, así que Saúl lo puso al mando de los hombres de guerra. Esto agradó a todo el pueblo y también a los oficiales de Saúl.
es.R: Saúl enviaba a David a muchas misiones, y David siempre las cumplía bien. Por eso Saúl lo hizo jefe de los soldados. Todo el pueblo se alegró de esto, y también los oficiales de Saúl.

fr.L: Et David sortait ; partout où Saül l’envoyait, il réussissait, et Saül le plaça à la tête des hommes de guerre. Et cela fut bon aux yeux de tout le peuple et aussi aux yeux des serviteurs de Saül.
fr.B: David partait partout où Saül l’envoyait, et il réussissait chaque fois ; aussi Saül le mit-il à la tête des hommes de guerre. Cela plut à tout le peuple, et aussi aux officiers de Saül.
fr.R: Saül a envoyé David en mission plusieurs fois, et chaque fois David a réussi. Alors Saül l’a nommé chef des soldats. Tout le peuple était content, et les officiers de Saül aussi.

sw.L: Daudi akatoka; kila mahali Sauli alipomtuma, alifanikiwa, naye Sauli akamweka juu ya watu wa vita. Ikawa vyema machoni pa watu wote na pia machoni pa watumishi wa Sauli.
sw.B: Daudi alikwenda kila mahali Sauli alipomtuma, akafanikiwa kila mara, hivyo Sauli akamweka kuwa mkuu wa askari. Jambo hili likawapendeza watu wote, na maafisa wa Sauli pia.
sw.R: Sauli alimtuma Daudi kwenda kufanya kazi nyingi, na kila mara Daudi alifanikiwa. Basi Sauli akamfanya kuwa kiongozi wa askari. Watu wote wakafurahi kwa jambo hili, na maafisa wa Sauli pia.

vi.L: Đa-vít đi ra; bất cứ nơi nào Sau-lơ sai ông đi, ông đều thành công, và Sau-lơ đặt ông chỉ huy các chiến binh. Điều đó tốt trong mắt toàn dân, và cả trong mắt các đầy tớ của Sau-lơ nữa.
vi.B: Sau-lơ sai Đa-vít đi đâu, ông cũng đi và lần nào cũng thành công, nên Sau-lơ giao cho ông chỉ huy quân binh. Việc ấy làm vừa lòng toàn dân, và cả các quần thần của Sau-lơ nữa.
vi.R: Sau-lơ sai Đa-vít đi làm nhiều việc, và lần nào Đa-vít cũng làm tốt. Vì vậy, Sau-lơ cho ông làm người chỉ huy quân lính. Toàn dân đều vui về việc này, và các quần thần của Sau-lơ cũng vậy.

ko.L: 그리고 다윗은 나갔다. 사울이 그를 보내는 곳마다 그는 일을 잘 해냈다. 그래서 사울이 그를 군인들 위에 세웠다. 그리고 그것이 모든 백성의 눈에 좋았고 사울의 신하들의 눈에도 좋았다.
ko.B: 다윗은 사울이 보내는 곳마다 나가서 언제나 일을 잘 해냈다. 그래서 사울은 그를 군인들을 거느리는 자리에 앉혔다. 온 백성이 이 일을 좋아했고, 사울의 신하들도 좋아했다.
ko.R: 사울은 다윗을 여러 번 싸움터에 내보냈는데, 다윗은 그때마다 일을 잘 해냈다. 그래서 사울은 다윗을 군대의 지휘관으로 삼았다. 모든 백성이 이 일을 기뻐했고, 사울의 신하들도 기뻐했다.

pt.L: E Davi saía; aonde quer que Saul o enviasse, ele era bem-sucedido, e Saul o pôs sobre os homens de guerra. E isso foi bom aos olhos de todo o povo e também aos olhos dos servos de Saul.
pt.B: Davi saía para onde Saul o mandasse e sempre se saía bem, por isso Saul o pôs no comando dos homens de guerra. Isso agradou a todo o povo e também aos oficiais de Saul.
pt.R: Saul mandava Davi em muitas missões, e Davi sempre se saía bem. Por isso Saul o fez chefe dos soldados. Todo o povo ficou contente com isso, e os oficiais de Saul também.

am.L: ዳዊትም ወጣ፤ ሳኦል በላከው ስፍራ ሁሉ ይከናወንለት ነበር፤ ሳኦልም በጦር ሰዎች ላይ ሾመው። ይህም በሕዝቡ ሁሉ ዓይን፣ ደግሞም በሳኦል ባሪያዎች ዓይን መልካም ሆነ።
am.B: ዳዊት ሳኦል ወደ ላከው ስፍራ ሁሉ ይወጣ ነበር፤ በሄደበትም ሁሉ ይሳካለት ነበር፤ ስለዚህ ሳኦል በተዋጊዎቹ ላይ ሾመው። ይህም ሕዝቡን ሁሉ፣ የሳኦልንም ሹማምንት ጭምር ደስ አሰኘ።
am.R: ሳኦል ዳዊትን ብዙ ጊዜ ለተለያዩ ተልእኮዎች ላከው፤ ዳዊትም ሁልጊዜ ይሳካለት ነበር። ስለዚህ ሳኦል በወታደሮቹ ላይ አለቃ አደረገው። ሕዝቡ ሁሉ በዚህ ደስ አላቸው፤ የሳኦልም ሹማምንት ደስ አላቸው።

decisions.choice: he succeeded: he acted wisely and so did well
decisions.reason: The verb means both acting with good sense and having success as a result. It is a key word of this chapter (verses 14, 15 and 30), and it shows David's skill as well as Yahweh's help (verse 14).

decisions.choice: the men of war: the soldiers
decisions.reason: The phrase means fighting men, the army Saul kept with him (13:2; 14:52).

decisions.choice: Saul's servants: the men of the king's court
decisions.reason: The "servants" of a king are his officials and officers, free men who serve at court (16:15-17; 22:6-9).

decisions.choice: Saul's officials
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "officials" for the king's servants, so that readers do not think of household slaves. Literal keeps "servants".

decisions.choice: réussir
decisions.reason: The key verb of the chapter (verses 5, 14, 15, 30) means both acting wisely and succeeding (m1); "réussir" is kept at every level so the repetition is heard, as the English "succeeded".

decisions.choice: "alifanikiwa"
decisions.reason: The verb means acting wisely and so succeeding (m1); "kufanikiwa" (to succeed) is used for it through the chapter (verses 14, 15, 30), as the English uses "succeed".

decisions.choice: era bem-sucedido (L); se saía bem (B, R)
decisions.reason: For the whole chapter (verses 14, 15, 30): the key verb, which joins acting wisely and doing well (m1), keeps one wording at each level so that the reader hears it return; the note keeps the sense of good judgment.

source.text: וַיְהִ֣י בְּבוֹאָ֗ם בְּשׁ֤וּב דָּוִד֙ מֵהַכּ֣וֹת אֶת־הַפְּלִשְׁתִּ֔י וַתֵּצֶ֨אנָה הַנָּשִׁ֜ים מִכָּל־עָרֵ֤י יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ לָשִׁ֣יר וְהַמְּחֹל֔וֹת לִקְרַ֖את שָׁא֣וּל הַמֶּ֑לֶךְ בְּתֻפִּ֥ים בְּשִׂמְחָ֖ה וּבְשָׁלִשִֽׁים׃

records.literal_gloss: And it was, when they came, when returned David from striking down the Philistine, and came out the women from all [the] cities of Israel to sing and the dances to meet Saul the king, with tambourines, with joy, and with three-stringed instruments.

en.L: And it happened, as they were coming, when David returned from striking down the Philistine, that the women came out from all the cities of Israel, singing and dancing, to meet Saul the king, with tambourines, with joy, and with three-stringed instruments.
en.B: As the army was coming home, when David returned from killing the Philistine, the women came out from every town in Israel to meet King Saul, singing and dancing with tambourines, with joyful songs and with musical instruments.
en.R: When the soldiers were coming home after David had killed the Philistine, women came out of all the towns of Israel to meet King Saul. They sang and danced with joy, and they played tambourines and other musical instruments.

es.L: Y sucedió que, cuando venían, cuando David volvía de matar al filisteo, salieron las mujeres de todas las ciudades de Israel cantando y danzando al encuentro del rey Saúl, con panderos, con alegría y con instrumentos de tres cuerdas.
es.B: Cuando el ejército volvía a casa, al regresar David de matar al filisteo, las mujeres salieron de todas las ciudades de Israel a recibir al rey Saúl, cantando y danzando con panderos, con cantos de alegría y con instrumentos musicales.
es.R: Cuando los soldados volvían a casa, después de que David mató al filisteo, salieron mujeres de todos los pueblos de Israel a recibir al rey Saúl. Cantaban y bailaban con alegría, y tocaban panderos y otros instrumentos musicales.

fr.L: Et il arriva, comme ils rentraient, quand David revint d’avoir frappé le Philistin, que les femmes sortirent de toutes les villes d’Israël en chantant et en dansant, à la rencontre du roi Saül, avec des tambourins, avec joie et avec des instruments à trois cordes.
fr.B: Comme l’armée rentrait, au retour de David après qu’il eut tué le Philistin, les femmes sortirent de toutes les villes d’Israël à la rencontre du roi Saül, en chantant et en dansant, avec des tambourins, des chants de joie et des instruments de musique.
fr.R: Les soldats rentraient chez eux après que David avait tué le Philistin. Alors des femmes sont sorties de toutes les villes d’Israël pour accueillir le roi Saül. Elles chantaient et dansaient de joie, et elles jouaient du tambourin et d’autres instruments de musique.

sw.L: Ikawa walipokuwa wakija, Daudi aliporudi kutoka kumpiga Mfilisti, wanawake wakatoka katika miji yote ya Israeli, wakiimba na kucheza, kumlaki mfalme Sauli, kwa matari, kwa furaha, na kwa vinanda vya nyuzi tatu.
sw.B: Jeshi lilipokuwa likirudi nyumbani, Daudi aliporudi kutoka kumwua Mfilisti, wanawake wakatoka katika kila mji wa Israeli kumlaki Mfalme Sauli, wakiimba na kucheza kwa matari, kwa nyimbo za furaha na kwa vyombo vya muziki.
sw.R: Askari walipokuwa wakirudi nyumbani baada ya Daudi kumwua Mfilisti, wanawake wakatoka katika miji yote ya Israeli kumlaki Mfalme Sauli. Wakaimba na kucheza kwa furaha, wakipiga matari na vyombo vingine vya muziki.

vi.L: Khi họ trở về, lúc Đa-vít trở về sau khi đánh hạ người Phi-li-tin, các phụ nữ từ tất cả các thành của Y-sơ-ra-ên đi ra, ca hát và nhảy múa, để đón vua Sau-lơ, với trống cơm, với niềm vui và với đàn ba dây.
vi.B: Khi quân đội trở về, lúc Đa-vít đã giết người Phi-li-tin trở về, các phụ nữ từ khắp các thành của Y-sơ-ra-ên kéo ra đón vua Sau-lơ, vừa ca hát vừa nhảy múa, với trống cơm, với những bài ca vui mừng và các nhạc cụ.
vi.R: Khi quân lính trở về, sau khi Đa-vít đã giết người Phi-li-tin, các phụ nữ từ khắp các thành của Y-sơ-ra-ên kéo ra đón vua Sau-lơ. Họ ca hát và nhảy múa mừng vui, đánh trống cơm và chơi các nhạc cụ khác.

ko.L: 그리고 그들이 돌아올 때, 곧 다윗이 그 블레셋 사람을 쳐 죽이고 돌아올 때, 이스라엘의 모든 성읍에서 여자들이 나와 노래하고 춤추며, 소고와 기쁨과 삼현금을 가지고 사울 왕을 맞았다.
ko.B: 군대가 돌아올 때, 곧 다윗이 그 블레셋 사람을 죽이고 돌아올 때, 이스라엘의 모든 성읍에서 여자들이 나와 소고를 치고 악기를 타며 즐겁게 노래하고 춤추면서 사울 왕을 맞았다.
ko.R: 다윗이 그 블레셋 사람을 죽인 뒤에 군인들이 집으로 돌아오고 있었다. 그때 이스라엘의 모든 마을에서 여자들이 사울 왕을 맞으러 나왔다. 그들은 기뻐하며 노래하고 춤을 추었다. 그리고 소고와 여러 악기를 연주했다.

pt.L: E aconteceu, quando eles vinham, quando Davi voltava de ferir o filisteu, que as mulheres saíram de todas as cidades de Israel, cantando e dançando, ao encontro do rei Saul, com tamborins, com alegria e com instrumentos de três cordas.
pt.B: Quando o exército voltava para casa, depois que Davi matou o filisteu, as mulheres saíram de todas as cidades de Israel ao encontro do rei Saul, cantando e dançando com tamborins, com canções de alegria e com instrumentos musicais.
pt.R: Quando os soldados estavam voltando para casa, depois que Davi matou o filisteu, mulheres saíram de todas as cidades de Israel para encontrar o rei Saul. Elas cantavam e dançavam de alegria e tocavam tamborins e outros instrumentos musicais.

am.L: እንዲህም ሆነ፤ እየመጡ ሳሉ፣ ዳዊት ፍልስጥኤማዊውን መትቶ በተመለሰ ጊዜ፣ ሴቶች እየዘመሩና እየጨፈሩ ንጉሡን ሳኦልን ለመቀበል ከእስራኤል ከተሞች ሁሉ ወጡ፤ በከበሮ፣ በደስታና ባለ ሦስት አውታር በሆኑ የዜማ መሣሪያዎች [ወጡ]።
am.B: ሠራዊቱ ወደ አገሩ ሲመለስ፣ ዳዊት ፍልስጥኤማዊውን ገድሎ በተመለሰ ጊዜ፣ ሴቶች ንጉሥ ሳኦልን ለመቀበል ከእስራኤል ከተሞች ሁሉ ወጡ፤ በከበሮ፣ በደስታ ዝማሬና በዜማ መሣሪያዎች እየዘመሩና እየጨፈሩ ወጡ።
am.R: ዳዊት ፍልስጥኤማዊውን ከገደለ በኋላ ወታደሮቹ ወደ አገራቸው እየተመለሱ ነበር። በዚያን ጊዜ ሴቶች ንጉሥ ሳኦልን ለመቀበል ከእስራኤል ከተሞች ሁሉ ወጡ። በደስታ ዘመሩ፤ ጨፈሩም፤ ከበሮና ሌሎች የዜማ መሣሪያዎችንም ተጫወቱ።

decisions.choice: the women came out singing and dancing: a victory welcome
decisions.reason: Women met returning warriors with songs, dances and tambourines (Exodus 15:20-21; Judges 11:34). The welcome is for the king and his army after the victory over the Philistines in chapter 17.

decisions.choice: when they came: the army coming home after the battle of chapter 17
decisions.reason: "They" are Saul's men returning from the pursuit of the Philistines (17:52-53). "The Philistine" is Goliath (17:50-51).

decisions.choice: three-stringed instruments: an instrument whose exact kind is not known
decisions.reason: The word comes from the number three. It may name a three-stringed lute, a triangle, cymbals, or a dance in three beats. It is found only here.

decisions.choice: musical instruments
decisions.reason: Since the exact instrument is not known, Balanced and Readable use a general term; Literal follows the word's link with "three".

decisions.choice: the army (Balanced); the soldiers (Readable)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says only "they". Balanced and Readable name who was coming.

decisions.choice: "vinanda vya nyuzi tatu" (L); "vyombo vya muziki" (B, R)
decisions.reason: The word comes from the number three and the exact instrument is unknown (m3); Literal keeps the "three", Balanced and Readable use a general term, as the English does.

decisions.choice: "trống cơm" for the tambourine; "đàn ba dây" (L), "nhạc cụ" (B, R)
decisions.reason: The instrument of the three strings is not known (m3); Literal keeps the Hebrew's description, the other levels say "instruments" as the English does.

decisions.choice: "삼현금" (three-stringed instrument) at Literal; "악기" (musical instruments) at Balanced and Readable
decisions.reason: The exact kind of instrument is not known (meaning decision m3); Literal keeps the Hebrew's "three" in the name, the other levels say "instruments", as the English does.

source.text: וַֽתַּעֲנֶ֛ינָה הַנָּשִׁ֥ים הַֽמְשַׂחֲק֖וֹת וַתֹּאמַ֑רְןָ הִכָּ֤ה שָׁאוּל֙ בַּאֲלָפָ֔יו וְדָוִ֖ד בְּרִבְבֹתָֽיו׃

records.literal_gloss: And sang the women who [were] playing, and they said, Struck down Saul his thousands, and David his ten thousands.

en.L: And the women who were celebrating sang to one another and said, \q "Saul has struck down his thousands, \q and David his ten thousands."
en.B: As they celebrated, the women sang to one another, \q "Saul has struck down his thousands, \q and David his tens of thousands."
en.R: As they celebrated, the women sang this song back and forth: \q "Saul has killed his thousands, \q and David his tens of thousands."

es.L: Y las mujeres que festejaban cantaban unas a otras, y decían: \q «Saúl ha abatido a sus miles, \q y David a sus decenas de miles».
es.B: Mientras celebraban, las mujeres cantaban unas a otras: \q «Saúl ha derribado a sus miles, \q y David a sus decenas de miles».
es.R: Mientras celebraban, las mujeres cantaban este canto, un grupo respondiendo al otro: \q «Saúl ha matado a sus miles, \q y David a sus decenas de miles».

fr.L: Et les femmes qui se réjouissaient chantaient en se répondant, et elles disaient : \q « Saül a frappé ses milliers, \q et David ses dizaines de milliers. »
fr.B: Tout en faisant la fête, les femmes chantaient en se répondant : \q « Saül a frappé ses milliers, \q et David ses dizaines de milliers. »
fr.R: Pendant la fête, les femmes chantaient ce chant en se répondant : \q « Saül a tué ses milliers, \q et David ses dizaines de milliers. »

sw.L: Wanawake waliokuwa wakishangilia wakaimba wakijibizana, wakasema, \q "Sauli amewapiga maelfu yake, \q na Daudi makumi elfu yake."
sw.B: Walipokuwa wakishangilia, wanawake waliimba wakijibizana, \q "Sauli amewapiga maelfu yake, \q na Daudi makumi ya maelfu yake."
sw.R: Walipokuwa wakishangilia, wanawake waliimba wimbo huu wakijibizana: \q "Sauli ameua maelfu yake, \q na Daudi makumi ya maelfu yake."

vi.L: Các phụ nữ đang vui chơi hát đối đáp với nhau và nói: \q "Sau-lơ đã đánh hạ hàng ngàn của mình, \q còn Đa-vít hàng vạn của mình."
vi.B: Trong lúc vui mừng, các phụ nữ hát đối đáp với nhau: \q "Sau-lơ giết hàng ngàn, \q còn Đa-vít giết hàng vạn."
vi.R: Trong lúc vui mừng, các phụ nữ hát đi hát lại bài ca này: \q "Sau-lơ giết được hàng ngàn, \q còn Đa-vít giết được hàng vạn."

ko.L: 그리고 흥겹게 노는 여자들이 서로 주고받으며 노래했다. \q "사울은 수천을 쳐 죽였고, \q 다윗은 수만을 [쳐 죽였다]."
ko.B: 여자들은 즐거워하며 서로 주고받으며 노래했다. \q "사울은 수천을 쳐 죽였고, \q 다윗은 수만을 쳐 죽였다."
ko.R: 여자들은 즐거워하며 이 노래를 서로 주고받으며 불렀다. \q "사울은 수천 명을 죽였고, \q 다윗은 수만 명을 죽였다."

pt.L: E as mulheres que festejavam cantavam umas para as outras e diziam: \q "Saul feriu os seus milhares, \q e Davi, os seus dez milhares."
pt.B: Enquanto festejavam, as mulheres cantavam umas para as outras: \q "Saul matou os seus milhares, \q e Davi, as suas dezenas de milhares."
pt.R: Enquanto festejavam, as mulheres cantavam esta canção, um grupo respondendo ao outro: \q "Saul matou os seus milhares, \q e Davi, as suas dezenas de milhares."

am.L: ይጫወቱ የነበሩትም ሴቶች እየተቀባበሉ ዘመሩ፤ እንዲህም አሉ፦ \q «ሳኦል ሺዎቹን መታ፤ \q ዳዊትም እልፎቹን።»
am.B: ሴቶቹ በደስታ ሲጫወቱ እየተቀባበሉ እንዲህ ብለው ዘመሩ፦ \q «ሳኦል ሺዎቹን መታ፤ \q ዳዊትም አሥር ሺዎቹን።»
am.R: ሴቶቹ በደስታ ሲጫወቱ ይህን መዝሙር እየተቀባበሉ ዘመሩ፦ \q «ሳኦል ሺዎችን ገደለ፤ \q ዳዊትም አሥር ሺዎችን።»

decisions.choice: sang: sang in turn, one group answering another
decisions.reason: The verb usually means "answer". Used of singing, it means a song sung in parts, one group of singers replying to another (Exodus 15:21; Ezra 3:11).

decisions.choice: who were celebrating: playing, dancing and making merry
decisions.reason: The verb means to play or laugh. Here it is the joyful dancing and music of a festival, as when David celebrates before Yahweh in 2 Samuel 6:5, 21.

decisions.choice: his thousands ... his ten thousands: a poetic pair that may praise both men
decisions.reason: "Thousand" and "ten thousand" are a common pair in Hebrew poetry, where the second line raises the first (Deuteronomy 32:30; Psalm 91:7; Micah 6:7). The women may mean that both men have won great victories. Saul hears the song as setting David above him (verse 8), and the Philistines remember it in the same way (21:12; 29:5).

decisions.choice: "Saul has struck down his thousands, and David his tens of thousands" at Balanced; Readable "killed"
decisions.reason: The song is quoted again in 21:12 and 29:5, so its wording is kept short and fixed at each level for those verses. Literal keeps "ten thousands" as the Hebrew plural; Balanced uses the English "tens of thousands". Each level sets the song in two lines after the line that introduces it.

decisions.choice: « Saül a frappé ses milliers, et David ses dizaines de milliers » (L, B); « Saül a tué ... » (R)
decisions.reason: The song comes back in 21:12 and 29:5, so its wording is fixed at each level, as the English (r-en-1); "dizaines de milliers" is plainer than the older "myriades".

decisions.choice: a sus miles ... a sus decenas de miles
decisions.reason: The women's song (m3), set in two lines as the English is, with “decenas de miles” for the Hebrew ten thousands; the same wording returns at 21:12 and 29:5.

decisions.choice: "Sauli amewapiga maelfu yake, na Daudi makumi (ya) elfu yake"
decisions.reason: The women's song is quoted again in 21:12 and 29:5, so its Swahili wording is fixed at each level and repeated there: "amewapiga" (has struck down) at Literal and Balanced, "ameua" (has killed) at Readable.

decisions.choice: "hàng ngàn ... hàng vạn"
decisions.reason: "vạn" (ten thousand) is the natural Vietnamese partner of "ngàn" in a poetic pair; the song is set in two lines as the English is, and the same wording returns at 21:12 and 29:5.

decisions.choice: "수천" / "수만" (thousands / tens of thousands), set in two lines as the English
decisions.reason: The women answer each other in a two-line song (meaning decisions m1, m3); "수천 ... 수만" keeps the rising pair in plain modern Korean, and avoids the wording of the older Korean Bibles.

decisions.choice: Saul matou os seus milhares, e Davi, as suas dezenas de milhares (B, R); Saul feriu os seus milhares, e Davi, os seus dez milhares (L)
alternatives: Saul matou mil, e Davi, dez mil
decisions.reason: For the whole book: the song returns in 21:12 and 29:5, so its wording is fixed here at each level, drafted from the Hebrew. Balanced says "matou", the plain sense of "struck down", with Readable; Literal keeps "feriu" and the Hebrew plural "dez milhares" (m3). The numbers stay in words, as poetry.

decisions.choice: "ሺዎቹን ... እልፎቹን" (L), "ሺዎቹን ... አሥር ሺዎቹን" (B), with "ዳዊትም" (and David) rather than "ዳዊት ግን" (but David)
decisions.reason: The two lines are a poetic pair; "-ም" keeps the parallel without making the song a contrast in itself, as the meaning note asks. "እልፍ" is the old word for ten thousand; Balanced and Readable say "አሥር ሺ" so every reader hears the number.

source.text: וַיִּ֨חַר לְשָׁא֜וּל מְאֹ֗ד וַיֵּ֤רַע בְּעֵינָיו֙ הַדָּבָ֣ר הַזֶּ֔ה וַיֹּ֗אמֶר נָתְנ֤וּ לְדָוִד֙ רְבָב֔וֹת וְלִ֥י נָתְנ֖וּ הָאֲלָפִ֑ים וְע֥וֹד ל֖וֹ אַ֥ךְ הַמְּלוּכָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And it burned to Saul greatly, and was evil in his eyes the thing the this, and he said, They have given to David ten thousands, and to me they have given the thousands, and still for him [is] only the kingdom.

en.L: And Saul was very angry, and this word was evil in his eyes, and he said, "They have given to David ten thousands, and to me they have given the thousands, and what more [is there] for him but the kingdom?"
en.B: Saul was furious, and this saying displeased him. "They have credited David with tens of thousands," he said, "and me with mere thousands. What more is left for him but the kingdom?"
en.R: Saul became very angry. He did not like this song at all. He said, "They say that David has killed tens of thousands, but I have killed only thousands. The only thing left for him to take is my kingdom!"

es.L: Y se enojó Saúl en gran manera, y le pareció mal a sus ojos esta palabra, y dijo: «A David le han dado decenas de miles, y a mí me han dado los miles; ¿qué más [hay] para él sino el reino?».
es.B: Saúl se enfureció, y este dicho le disgustó. «A David le atribuyen decenas de miles», dijo, «y a mí apenas miles. ¿Qué más le queda sino el reino?».
es.R: Saúl se enojó mucho. No le gustó nada esa canción. Dijo: «Dicen que David ha matado a decenas de miles, pero yo solo a miles. ¡Lo único que le falta es quitarme el reino!».

fr.L: Et Saül fut très irrité, et cette parole fut mauvaise à ses yeux, et il dit : « Ils ont donné à David des dizaines de milliers, et à moi ils ont donné les milliers ; que lui [reste-t-il] encore, sinon la royauté ? »
fr.B: Saül entra dans une violente colère, car ces paroles lui déplurent. « On a attribué à David des dizaines de milliers, dit-il, et à moi de simples milliers. Que lui manque-t-il encore, sinon la royauté ? »
fr.R: Saül s’est mis très en colère. Ce chant ne lui plaisait pas du tout. Il a dit : « Elles disent que David a tué des dizaines de milliers d’hommes, et moi seulement des milliers. Il ne lui manque plus que de prendre mon royaume ! »

sw.L: Sauli akakasirika sana, na neno hili likawa baya machoni pake, akasema, "Wamempa Daudi makumi elfu, na mimi wamenipa maelfu; na zaidi ya hayo amebakiwa na nini ila ufalme?"
sw.B: Sauli akakasirika mno, na maneno hayo hayakumpendeza. Akasema, "Wamempa Daudi makumi ya maelfu, nami wamenipa maelfu tu. Amebakiwa na nini tena ila ufalme?"
sw.R: Sauli akakasirika sana. Hakuupenda wimbo huo hata kidogo. Akasema, "Wanasema kwamba Daudi ameua makumi ya maelfu, lakini mimi nimeua maelfu tu. Kilichobaki kwake ni kuuchukua ufalme wangu tu!"

vi.L: Sau-lơ rất giận, và lời ấy là điều xấu trong mắt ông. Ông nói: "Họ cho Đa-vít hàng vạn, còn cho ta thì hàng ngàn; nó còn thiếu gì nữa ngoài vương quốc?"
vi.B: Sau-lơ vô cùng tức giận, và câu hát ấy làm ông khó chịu. Ông nói: "Họ gán cho Đa-vít hàng vạn, còn ta thì chỉ hàng ngàn. Nó còn thiếu gì nữa ngoài ngôi vua?"
vi.R: Sau-lơ rất tức giận. Ông không thích bài hát ấy chút nào. Ông nói: "Họ nói Đa-vít giết được hàng vạn, còn ta chỉ giết được hàng ngàn. Điều duy nhất còn lại cho nó là lấy ngôi vua của ta!"

ko.L: 그리고 사울이 몹시 화가 났고, 이 말이 그의 눈에 악하게 보였다. 그가 말했다. "그들이 다윗에게는 수만을 돌리고 나에게는 수천을 돌렸으니, 그에게 더 남은 것은 왕국뿐이 아니냐?"
ko.B: 사울은 몹시 화가 났다. 이 노래가 무척 못마땅했다. 그가 말했다. "다윗에게는 수만 명을 돌리고, 나에게는 겨우 수천 명을 돌리는구나. 이제 그가 더 얻을 것은 왕의 자리밖에 없지 않으냐?"
ko.R: 사울은 몹시 화가 났다. 그는 이 노래가 정말 싫었다. 사울이 말했다. "사람들이 다윗은 수만 명을 죽였다고 하고, 나는 겨우 수천 명을 죽였다고 하는구나. 이제 다윗이 가질 것은 내 나라밖에 남지 않았다!"

pt.L: E Saul se irou muito, e esta palavra foi má aos seus olhos, e ele disse: "Deram a Davi dez milhares, e a mim deram os milhares; e o que mais [há] para ele senão o reino?"
pt.B: Saul ficou furioso, e aquelas palavras lhe desagradaram. "Atribuíram a Davi dezenas de milhares", disse ele, "e a mim, apenas milhares. O que mais falta para ele, senão o reino?"
pt.R: Saul ficou com muita raiva. Não gostou nada daquela canção. Ele disse: "Elas dizem que Davi matou dezenas de milhares, mas que eu matei só milhares. A única coisa que falta para ele tomar é o meu reino!"

am.L: ሳኦልም እጅግ ተቆጣ፤ ይህም ነገር በዓይኑ ክፉ ሆነ፤ እንዲህም አለ፦ «ለዳዊት እልፎችን ሰጡት፤ ለእኔ ግን ሺዎችን ሰጡኝ፤ ከመንግሥቱ በቀር ሌላ ምን ቀረው?»
am.B: ሳኦል እጅግ ተናደደ፤ ይህም አነጋገር አላስደሰተውም። «ለዳዊት አሥር ሺዎችን ቆጠሩለት» አለ፤ «ለእኔ ግን ሺዎችን ብቻ። እንግዲህ ከመንግሥቱ በቀር ሌላ ምን ቀረው?»
am.R: ሳኦል በጣም ተቆጣ። ይህ መዝሙር ፈጽሞ አላስደሰተውም። እንዲህም አለ፦ «ዳዊት አሥር ሺዎችን ገደለ ይላሉ፤ እኔ ግን ሺዎችን ብቻ ገደልኩ። እንግዲህ የቀረው መንግሥቴን መውሰድ ብቻ ነው!»

decisions.choice: it burned to Saul: Saul became angry
decisions.reason: The Hebrew speaks of anger as burning or heat (11:6; 20:30).

decisions.choice: and still for him only the kingdom: what more can he get except the kingdom?
decisions.reason: The words are short and sharp: "and still for him only the kingdom." Saul means that the people have given David everything except the throne, and that the throne will be next. He does not know of David's anointing (16:13), but Samuel had told him that Yahweh would give the kingdom to someone better than he (15:28).

decisions.choice: they have given: they have credited, ascribed
decisions.reason: "Given" here means "assigned in the song": the women have given David the larger number.

decisions.choice: a question: "What more is left for him but the kingdom?"
decisions.reason: The Hebrew is a statement, but English says this most naturally as a question. Readable keeps it a statement.

decisions.choice: mere thousands
decisions.reason: Balanced adds "mere" to bring out the contrast Saul draws between the two numbers.

source.text: וַיְהִ֥י שָׁא֖וּל עוֹיֵ֣ן אֶת־דָּוִ֑ד מֵהַיּ֥וֹם הַה֖וּא וָהָֽלְאָה׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And was Saul eyeing David from the day the that and onward.

en.L: And Saul was eyeing David from that day and onward.
en.B: From that day on, Saul watched David with suspicion.
en.R: From that day on, Saul watched David closely because he did not trust him.

es.L: Y Saúl miraba con recelo a David desde aquel día en adelante.
es.B: Desde aquel día, Saúl vigilaba a David con desconfianza.
es.R: Desde aquel día, Saúl vigilaba de cerca a David porque no confiaba en él.

fr.L: Et Saül eut l’œil sur David à partir de ce jour-là et dans la suite.
fr.B: À partir de ce jour, Saül regarda David d’un œil soupçonneux.
fr.R: À partir de ce jour-là, Saül a surveillé David de près, parce qu’il n’avait pas confiance en lui.

sw.L: Sauli akamtazama Daudi kwa jicho baya tangu siku ile na kuendelea.
sw.B: Tangu siku ile, Sauli alimtazama Daudi kwa mashaka.
sw.R: Tangu siku ile, Sauli alimchunguza Daudi kwa karibu, kwa sababu hakumwamini.

vi.L: Từ ngày đó trở đi, Sau-lơ để mắt dò xét Đa-vít.
vi.B: Từ ngày đó trở đi, Sau-lơ nhìn Đa-vít với con mắt nghi kỵ.
vi.R: Từ ngày đó trở đi, Sau-lơ theo dõi Đa-vít rất kỹ, vì vua không tin ông.

ko.L: 그리고 사울은 그날부터 계속 다윗을 눈여겨보았다.
ko.B: 그날부터 사울은 다윗을 의심의 눈으로 지켜보았다.
ko.R: 그날부터 사울은 다윗을 믿지 못하고 늘 지켜보았다.

pt.L: E Saul ficou de olho em Davi daquele dia em diante.
pt.B: Daquele dia em diante, Saul passou a vigiar Davi com desconfiança.
pt.R: Daquele dia em diante, Saul ficou vigiando Davi de perto, porque não confiava nele.

am.L: ሳኦልም ከዚያ ቀን ጀምሮ ወደ ፊትም ዳዊትን በዓይኑ ይከታተለው ነበር።
am.B: ከዚያ ቀን ጀምሮ ሳኦል ዳዊትን በጥርጣሬ ዓይን ይመለከተው ጀመር።
am.R: ከዚያ ቀን ጀምሮ ሳኦል ዳዊትን ስላላመነው በቅርብ ይከታተለው ጀመር።

decisions.choice: eyeing: watching with suspicion and jealousy
decisions.reason: The verb, found only here, is made from the word for "eye". It means to keep an eye on someone with distrust. The written Hebrew letters and the way the text is read aloud differ slightly here, but both give this sense.

decisions.choice: because he did not trust him
decisions.reason: Readable spells out the suspicion in the rare verb.

source.text: וַיְהִ֣י מִֽמָּחֳרָ֗ת וַתִּצְלַ֣ח רוּחַ֩ אֱלֹהִ֨ים׀רָעָ֤ה׀אֶל־שָׁאוּל֙ וַיִּתְנַבֵּ֣א בְתוֹךְ־הַבַּ֔יִת וְדָוִ֛ד מְנַגֵּ֥ן בְּיָד֖וֹ כְּי֣וֹם׀בְּי֑וֹם וְהַחֲנִ֖ית בְּיַד־שָׁאֽוּל׃

records.literal_gloss: And it was on [the] next day, and rushed [a] spirit of God evil upon Saul, and he prophesied in [the] midst of the house, and David [was] playing with his hand as day by day, and the spear [was] in [the] hand of Saul.

en.L: And it happened on the next day that an evil spirit of God rushed upon Saul, and he prophesied in the midst of the house, while David [was] playing with his hand, as day by day; and the spear [was] in Saul's hand.
en.B: The next day a harmful spirit from God rushed upon Saul, and he raved inside the house while David was playing the lyre, as he did every day. Saul had his spear in his hand.
en.R: The next day God let an evil spirit take hold of Saul. Saul began to act wildly inside his house, like a man in a trance. David was playing music on the lyre, as he did every day. Saul was holding a spear.

es.L: Y sucedió al día siguiente que un espíritu malo de Dios vino con poder sobre Saúl, y profetizaba en medio de la casa, mientras David tocaba con su mano, como día tras día; y la lanza [estaba] en la mano de Saúl.
es.B: Al día siguiente, un espíritu malo de parte de Dios vino con poder sobre Saúl, y él deliraba dentro de la casa mientras David tocaba la lira, como hacía cada día. Saúl tenía la lanza en la mano.
es.R: Al día siguiente, Dios dejó que un espíritu malo se apoderara de Saúl. Saúl comenzó a actuar como loco dentro de su casa, como un hombre en trance. David estaba tocando música con la lira, como lo hacía todos los días. Saúl tenía una lanza en la mano.

fr.L: Et il arriva, le lendemain, qu’un esprit de Dieu, mauvais, fondit sur Saül, et il prophétisa au milieu de la maison, tandis que David jouait de sa main, comme chaque jour ; et la lance [était] dans la main de Saül.
fr.B: Le lendemain, un esprit mauvais venant de Dieu fondit sur Saül, et il se mit à délirer dans la maison pendant que David jouait de la lyre, comme il le faisait chaque jour. Saül avait sa lance à la main.
fr.R: Le lendemain, Dieu a permis qu’un esprit mauvais s’empare de Saül. Saül s’est mis à s’agiter comme un fou dans sa maison, comme un homme en transe. David jouait de la lyre, comme tous les jours. Saül tenait une lance.

sw.L: Ikawa siku iliyofuata roho mbaya ya Mungu ikamjia Sauli kwa nguvu, naye akatabiri ndani ya nyumba, Daudi alipokuwa akipiga kwa mkono wake kama siku kwa siku; na mkuki [ulikuwa] mkononi mwa Sauli.
sw.B: Siku iliyofuata, roho mbaya kutoka kwa Mungu ikamjia Sauli kwa nguvu, akapayuka ndani ya nyumba, Daudi alipokuwa akipiga kinubi kama alivyofanya kila siku. Sauli alikuwa ameshika mkuki mkononi.
sw.R: Siku iliyofuata, Mungu aliiacha roho mbaya imshike Sauli. Sauli akaanza kufanya mambo ya kiwazimu ndani ya nyumba yake, kama mtu aliyepagawa. Daudi alikuwa akipiga kinubi, kama alivyofanya kila siku. Sauli alikuwa ameshika mkuki.

vi.L: Ngày hôm sau, một ác thần của Đức Chúa Trời giáng mạnh trên Sau-lơ, và ông nói tiên tri ở giữa nhà, trong khi Đa-vít lấy tay gảy đàn như mọi ngày; và cây giáo [ở] trong tay Sau-lơ.
vi.B: Ngày hôm sau, một ác thần từ Đức Chúa Trời giáng mạnh trên Sau-lơ, và ông nói năng cuồng loạn trong nhà, trong khi Đa-vít gảy đàn lia như mọi ngày. Sau-lơ cầm cây giáo trong tay.
vi.R: Ngày hôm sau, Đức Chúa Trời để cho một ác thần nắm lấy Sau-lơ. Sau-lơ bắt đầu cư xử điên cuồng trong nhà, như người bị nhập. Đa-vít đang gảy đàn lia như mọi ngày. Sau-lơ đang cầm một cây giáo.

ko.L: 그리고 그 이튿날, 하나님께로부터 [온] 악한 영이 사울에게 크게 임하여, 그가 집 안에서 예언했다. 다윗은 날마다 하던 대로 손으로 [수금을] 타고 있었고, 사울의 손에는 창이 [있었다].
ko.B: 이튿날 하나님께서 보내신 악한 영이 사울에게 크게 임하자, 그는 집 안에서 미친 듯이 날뛰었다. 다윗은 날마다 하던 대로 수금을 타고 있었다. 사울의 손에는 창이 들려 있었다.
ko.R: 이튿날 하나님께서 악한 영이 사울을 사로잡게 하셨다. 사울은 집 안에서 정신을 잃은 사람처럼 마구 날뛰었다. 다윗은 날마다 하던 대로 수금을 연주하고 있었다. 사울은 손에 창을 들고 있었다.

pt.L: E aconteceu, no dia seguinte, que um espírito mau de Deus irrompeu sobre Saul, e ele profetizou no meio da casa, enquanto Davi tocava com a sua mão, como dia após dia; e a lança [estava] na mão de Saul.
pt.B: No dia seguinte, um espírito mau da parte de Deus veio com força sobre Saul, e ele começou a delirar dentro de casa, enquanto Davi tocava a lira, como fazia todos os dias. Saul tinha a lança na mão.
pt.R: No dia seguinte, Deus deixou que um espírito mau tomasse conta de Saul. Saul começou a agir como louco dentro de casa, como alguém em transe. Davi estava tocando lira, como fazia todos os dias. Saul estava segurando uma lança.

am.L: በማግሥቱም እንዲህ ሆነ፤ ከእግዚአብሔር [የመጣ] ክፉ መንፈስ በሳኦል ላይ በኃይል መጣ፤ እርሱም በቤቱ መካከል ትንቢት ተናገረ፤ ዳዊትም እንደ ዕለት ዕለቱ በእጁ ይደረድር ነበር፤ ጦሩም በሳኦል እጅ ነበር።
am.B: በማግሥቱ ከእግዚአብሔር ዘንድ ክፉ መንፈስ በሳኦል ላይ በኃይል መጣ፤ እርሱም በቤቱ ውስጥ ይቃዥ ጀመር፤ ዳዊት ደግሞ እንደ ወትሮው በገና ይደረድር ነበር። ሳኦልም ጦሩን በእጁ ይዞ ነበር።
am.R: በማግሥቱ እግዚአብሔር ክፉ መንፈስ ሳኦልን እንዲይዘው ፈቀደ። ሳኦልም በቤቱ ውስጥ እንደ ተመሰጠ ሰው ያልተለመደ ነገር ያደርግ ጀመር። ዳዊት እንደ ሁልጊዜው በገና እየደረደረ ነበር። ሳኦል በእጁ ጦር ይዞ ነበር።

decisions.choice: an evil spirit of God: a harmful spirit that came from God
decisions.reason: Since Yahweh's Spirit left Saul, a spirit "from Yahweh" troubled him (16:14-16, 23; 19:9). The word "evil" can mean morally bad, or harmful and troubling. The text says that God sent it as part of his judgment on Saul (15:23, 28), as he sent an evil spirit between Abimelech and the men of Shechem (Judges 9:23). It does not say what kind of being it was.

decisions.choice: rushed upon Saul: the same verb as when God's Spirit came on Saul for good
decisions.reason: The verb "rushed" was used when the Spirit of God came on Saul so that he prophesied and led Israel (10:6, 10; 11:6), and when the Spirit of Yahweh came on David (16:13). Now a harmful spirit rushes on Saul in the same way.

decisions.choice: he prophesied: he behaved in an uncontrolled, frenzied way
decisions.reason: The verb is the one used for prophesying, but here it describes the outward behavior of someone gripped by a spirit, speaking and acting out of control (compare 10:10-11; 19:23-24). It does not mean that Saul brought a message from God.

decisions.choice: playing with his hand: playing the lyre
decisions.reason: David had been brought to court to play the lyre when the spirit troubled Saul, and the music brought Saul relief (16:16, 23). Saul's spear was a sign of his rank and was always near him (22:6; 26:7).

decisions.choice: raved (Balanced); act wildly ... like a man in a trance (Readable); the lyre
decisions.reason: "Prophesied" would suggest to most readers that Saul spoke a message from God, which is not the point here, so Balanced and Readable describe the behavior. They name the lyre from 16:16, 23. Literal keeps "prophesied".

decisions.choice: God let an evil spirit take hold of Saul
decisions.reason: Readable makes God the subject to show that the spirit came from him, as 16:14 says.

decisions.choice: délirer (B); s'agiter comme un fou, comme un homme en transe (R); prophétisa (L)
decisions.reason: As the English (r-en-1): "prophétiser" would make French readers think Saul gave a message from God, which is not the point (m3); Literal keeps the Hebrew verb.

decisions.choice: deliraba (B); actuar como loco ... en trance (R)
decisions.reason: “Prophesied” here means frenzied, uncontrolled behavior (m3). Literal keeps “profetizaba”; Balanced and Readable say what Saul did, as the English “raved” and “act wildly” (r-en-1).

decisions.choice: "akatabiri" (L); "akapayuka" (B); "kufanya mambo ya kiwazimu" (R)
decisions.reason: The verb of prophesying here describes frenzied behaviour (m3); Literal keeps "kutabiri", Balanced says "kupayuka" (to rave), and Readable describes it, as the English does.

decisions.choice: "nói tiên tri" (L); "nói năng cuồng loạn" (B); "cư xử điên cuồng" (R)
decisions.reason: The verb is the one for prophesying, but here it means frenzied, uncontrolled behaviour (m3); Literal keeps the verb, the other levels say what Saul did.

decisions.choice: "미친 듯이 날뛰었다" (raved) at Balanced and Readable; Literal keeps "예언했다" (prophesied)
decisions.reason: The verb here describes uncontrolled, frenzied behaviour (meaning decision m3), not speaking God's word; Literal keeps the Hebrew verb so that the link with 10:10 and 19:20-24 stays visible.

decisions.choice: irrompeu sobre ... profetizou (L); veio com força sobre ... começou a delirar (B)
decisions.reason: The verb of 16:13 returns (m2), so Literal and Balanced use the same words as there, "irrompeu" and "veio com força". Literal keeps "profetizou"; Balanced says "delirar" for the frenzy the verb describes here (m3), as the English says "raved". "Um espírito mau", as in 16:14.

source.text: וַיָּ֤טֶל שָׁאוּל֙ אֶֽת־הַחֲנִ֔ית וַיֹּ֕אמֶר אַכֶּ֥ה בְדָוִ֖ד וּבַקִּ֑יר וַיִּסֹּ֥ב דָּוִ֛ד מִפָּנָ֖יו פַּעֲמָֽיִם׃

records.literal_gloss: And hurled Saul the spear and said, I will strike David and the wall; and went around David from before him two times.

en.L: And Saul hurled the spear, and he said [to himself], "I will strike David to the wall." And David turned aside from before him twice.
en.B: Saul hurled the spear, thinking, "I will pin David to the wall." But David escaped from him twice.
en.R: Saul threw the spear at David. He thought, "I will pin David to the wall!" But David got out of the way. This happened two times.

es.L: Y arrojó Saúl la lanza, y dijo [para sí]: «Clavaré a David en la pared». Y David se le escabulló dos veces.
es.B: Saúl arrojó la lanza, pensando: «Voy a clavar a David en la pared». Pero David se le escapó dos veces.
es.R: Saúl le arrojó la lanza a David. Pensaba: «¡Voy a clavar a David en la pared!». Pero David la esquivó. Esto pasó dos veces.

fr.L: Et Saül lança la lance, et il dit [en lui-même] : « Je clouerai David au mur. » Et David s’écarta de devant lui à deux reprises.
fr.B: Saül lança la lance en pensant : « Je vais clouer David au mur. » Mais David l’esquiva par deux fois.
fr.R: Saül a lancé la lance sur David. Il pensait : « Je vais clouer David au mur ! » Mais David s’est écarté. Cela s’est passé deux fois.

sw.L: Sauli akautupa mkuki, akasema, "Nitampiga Daudi hadi ukutani." Daudi akaepuka mbele yake mara mbili.
sw.B: Sauli akautupa mkuki, akiwaza, "Nitamchoma Daudi na kumbana ukutani." Lakini Daudi akamponyoka mara mbili.
sw.R: Sauli akamtupia Daudi mkuki. Aliwaza, "Nitamchoma Daudi na kumbana ukutani!" Lakini Daudi akaukwepa. Jambo hili lilitokea mara mbili.

vi.L: Sau-lơ phóng cây giáo và nói [trong lòng]: "Ta sẽ ghim Đa-vít vào tường." Nhưng Đa-vít tránh khỏi ông hai lần.
vi.B: Sau-lơ phóng cây giáo, nghĩ thầm: "Ta sẽ ghim Đa-vít vào tường." Nhưng Đa-vít tránh được hai lần.
vi.R: Sau-lơ phóng cây giáo vào Đa-vít. Vua nghĩ: "Ta sẽ ghim nó vào tường!" Nhưng Đa-vít né được. Việc này xảy ra hai lần.

ko.L: 그리고 사울이 창을 던지며 말했다. "내가 다윗을 벽에 박아 버리겠다." 그러나 다윗은 그 앞에서 두 번이나 몸을 피했다.
ko.B: 사울은 "다윗을 벽에 박아 버리겠다" 하고 생각하며 창을 던졌다. 그러나 다윗은 두 번이나 그를 피했다.
ko.R: 사울은 다윗에게 창을 던지면서 생각했다. "다윗을 벽에 꽂아 버려야지!" 그러나 다윗은 몸을 피했다. 이런 일이 두 번이나 있었다.

pt.L: E Saul arremessou a lança e disse [consigo]: "Ferirei Davi na parede." E Davi se desviou de diante dele duas vezes.
pt.B: Saul arremessou a lança, pensando: "Vou cravar Davi na parede." Mas Davi escapou dele duas vezes.
pt.R: Saul atirou a lança em Davi. Ele pensou: "Vou prender Davi na parede!" Mas Davi saiu do caminho. Isso aconteceu duas vezes.

am.L: ሳኦልም ጦሩን ወረወረ፤ [በልቡም]፦ «ዳዊትን ከግድግዳው ጋር አጣብቄ እመታዋለሁ» አለ። ዳዊትም ከፊቱ ሁለት ጊዜ ዘወር አለ።
am.B: ሳኦል «ዳዊትን ከግድግዳው ጋር አጣብቀዋለሁ» ብሎ በማሰብ ጦሩን ወረወረ። ዳዊት ግን ሁለት ጊዜ ከእርሱ አመለጠ።
am.R: ሳኦል ጦሩን በዳዊት ላይ ወረወረ። በልቡም «ዳዊትን ከግድግዳው ጋር አጣብቀዋለሁ!» ብሎ አሰበ። ዳዊት ግን ዘወር ብሎ አመለጠ። ይህም ሁለት ጊዜ ሆነ።

decisions.choice: he said: he thought to himself
decisions.reason: "Said" here means said in his mind, as often in Hebrew (verses 17 and 21; Genesis 26:9). "Strike David and the wall" means to drive the spear through David into the wall (19:10).

decisions.choice: hurled: threw the spear
decisions.reason: The verb means to throw or cast. Saul throws his spear again at David in 19:10 and at Jonathan in 20:33.

decisions.choice: David turned aside from before him twice: he dodged the spear two times
decisions.reason: "Turned aside" means that David moved out of the spear's way. "Twice" may count this attack and the one in 19:10, which this verse tells in advance, or two throws on this one day.

decisions.choice: thinking (Balanced); He thought (Readable)
decisions.reason: Saul is speaking to himself, not to David, so Balanced and Readable say "thought". Literal adds "[to himself]".

source.text: וַיִּרָ֥א שָׁא֖וּל מִלִּפְנֵ֣י דָוִ֑ד כִּֽי־הָיָ֤ה יְהוָה֙ עִמּ֔וֹ וּמֵעִ֥ם שָׁא֖וּל סָֽר׃

records.literal_gloss: And was afraid Saul from before David, because was Yahweh with him, and from with Saul he had turned aside.

en.L: And Saul was afraid of David, because {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} was with him, but from Saul {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had turned away.
en.B: Saul feared David, because {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} was with David and had turned away from Saul.
en.R: Saul was afraid of David. He could see that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} was with David, but that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had left Saul.

es.L: Y tuvo miedo Saúl de David, porque {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} estaba con él, pero de Saúl se había apartado.
es.B: Saúl temía a David, porque {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} estaba con David y se había apartado de Saúl.
es.R: Saúl le tenía miedo a David. Veía que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} estaba con David, pero que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} había dejado a Saúl.

fr.L: Et Saül eut peur de David, parce que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} était avec lui, alors qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} s’était retiré de Saül.
fr.B: Saül craignait David, parce que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} était avec David et s’était retiré de Saül.
fr.R: Saül avait peur de David. Il voyait bien que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} était avec David, mais que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} avait quitté Saül.

sw.L: Sauli akamwogopa Daudi, kwa sababu {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alikuwa pamoja naye, lakini alikuwa amemwacha Sauli.
sw.B: Sauli akamwogopa Daudi, kwa sababu {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alikuwa pamoja na Daudi, naye alikuwa amemwacha Sauli.
sw.R: Sauli alimwogopa Daudi. Aliona kwamba {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alikuwa pamoja na Daudi, lakini {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alikuwa amemwacha Sauli.

vi.L: Sau-lơ sợ Đa-vít, vì {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} ở với ông, còn {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã lìa khỏi Sau-lơ.
vi.B: Sau-lơ sợ Đa-vít, vì {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} ở với Đa-vít và đã lìa bỏ Sau-lơ.
vi.R: Sau-lơ sợ Đa-vít. Vua thấy rằng {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} ở với Đa-vít, còn {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đã lìa bỏ mình.

ko.L: 그리고 사울이 다윗을 두려워했다. {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 그와 함께 계시고 사울에게서는 떠나셨기 때문이다.
ko.B: 사울은 다윗을 두려워했다. {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 다윗과 함께 계시고 사울에게서는 떠나셨기 때문이다.
ko.R: 사울은 다윗이 두려웠다. {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 다윗과 함께 계시고 사울에게서는 떠나셨다는 것을 사울도 알 수 있었다.

pt.L: E Saul teve medo de Davi, porque {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} estava com ele, mas de Saul {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} tinha se afastado.
pt.B: Saul tinha medo de Davi, porque {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} estava com Davi e tinha se afastado de Saul.
pt.R: Saul tinha medo de Davi. Ele percebia que {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} estava com Davi, mas que {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} tinha deixado Saul.

am.L: ሳኦልም ዳዊትን ፈራ፤ {{divine_name:እግዚአብሔር|ያህዌ}} ከእርሱ ጋር ነበርና፤ ከሳኦል ግን ተለይቶ ነበር።
am.B: {{divine_name:እግዚአብሔር|ያህዌ}} ከዳዊት ጋር ስለ ነበረና ከሳኦል ስለ ተለየ ሳኦል ዳዊትን ፈራ።
am.R: ሳኦል ዳዊትን ፈራ። {{divine_name:እግዚአብሔር|ያህዌ}} ከዳዊት ጋር እንደ ሆነ፣ {{divine_name:እግዚአብሔር|ያህዌ}} ግን ሳኦልን እንደ ተወው ያይ ነበር።

decisions.choice: Yahweh was with David but had turned away from Saul
decisions.reason: "Yahweh is with him" was said of David when he first came to court (16:18) and is repeated in verses 14 and 28. The same verb "turn away" was used in 16:14, when the Spirit of Yahweh left Saul. Saul now sees what Samuel said would happen (15:28).

decisions.choice: afraid: Saul fears David
decisions.reason: The king fears the young man he has put in charge of his soldiers. The fear grows through the chapter: "dreaded" in verse 15, "even more afraid" in verse 29.

decisions.choice: with David ... from Saul
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable repeat the names where the Hebrew uses pronouns, so that it is clear who is meant.

decisions.choice: He could see that
decisions.reason: Readable adds that Saul recognized this, as verse 28 says.

decisions.choice: tinha se afastado
decisions.reason: Literal and Balanced use "se afastar", the verb used in 16:14 when the Spirit of the LORD left Saul, to keep the echo (m1); Readable says "deixado", as there.

source.text: וַיְסִרֵ֤הוּ שָׁאוּל֙ מֵֽעִמּ֔וֹ וַיְשִׂמֵ֥הוּ ל֖וֹ שַׂר־אָ֑לֶף וַיֵּצֵ֥א וַיָּבֹ֖א לִפְנֵ֥י הָעָֽם׃פ

records.literal_gloss: And removed him Saul from with him and appointed him for himself [as] commander of [a] thousand, and he went out and came in before the people.

en.L: And Saul removed him from his presence and made him commander of a thousand for himself, and he went out and came in before the people.
en.B: So Saul sent him away from his presence and made him commander of a thousand men. David led the army in its campaigns.
en.R: So Saul sent David away from his court and made him commander of a thousand soldiers. David led the soldiers when they went out to fight and when they came home.

es.L: Y lo apartó Saúl de su lado, y lo puso como jefe de mil para sí; y salía y entraba delante del pueblo.
es.B: Así que Saúl lo alejó de su presencia y lo nombró jefe de mil hombres. David dirigía al ejército en sus campañas.
es.R: Así que Saúl alejó a David de su corte y lo nombró jefe de mil soldados. David dirigía a los soldados cuando salían a pelear y cuando volvían a casa.

fr.L: Et Saül l’écarta d’auprès de lui, et il l’établit pour lui chef de mille, et il sortait et rentrait devant le peuple.
fr.B: Saül l’éloigna donc de lui et le nomma chef de mille hommes. David conduisait l’armée dans ses campagnes.
fr.R: Alors Saül a éloigné David de sa cour et il l’a nommé chef de mille soldats. David conduisait les soldats quand ils partaient se battre et quand ils revenaient.

sw.L: Sauli akamwondoa mbele yake, akamfanya kuwa mkuu wa elfu kwa ajili yake, naye akatoka na kuingia mbele ya watu.
sw.B: Basi Sauli akamwondoa mbele yake, akamfanya kuwa mkuu wa askari elfu. Daudi akaliongoza jeshi katika vita vyake.
sw.R: Basi Sauli akamwondoa Daudi katika jumba lake la kifalme, akamfanya kuwa mkuu wa askari elfu. Daudi aliwaongoza askari walipotoka kwenda vitani na waliporudi nyumbani.

vi.L: Sau-lơ cho ông rời khỏi mình và lập ông làm chỉ huy ngàn người cho mình; ông ra vào trước mặt dân chúng.
vi.B: Vì vậy Sau-lơ cho Đa-vít rời khỏi cung và lập ông làm chỉ huy một ngàn quân. Đa-vít dẫn quân ra trận.
vi.R: Vì vậy Sau-lơ cho Đa-vít rời khỏi triều đình và lập ông làm chỉ huy một ngàn quân lính. Đa-vít dẫn quân lính ra trận và đưa họ trở về.

ko.L: 그리고 사울이 그를 자기 곁에서 떠나게 하고 그를 천부장으로 세웠다. 그래서 그는 백성 앞에서 나가고 들어왔다.
ko.B: 그래서 사울은 다윗을 곁에서 떠나보내고 천 명을 거느리는 지휘관으로 삼았다. 다윗은 군대를 이끌고 싸움터에 나갔다가 돌아오곤 했다.
ko.R: 그래서 사울은 다윗을 궁에서 내보내고 군인 천 명을 거느리는 지휘관으로 삼았다. 다윗은 군인들이 싸우러 나갈 때나 집으로 돌아올 때나 그들을 이끌었다.

pt.L: E Saul o afastou de junto de si e o fez para si comandante de mil, e ele saía e entrava diante do povo.
pt.B: Por isso Saul o afastou da sua presença e o fez comandante de mil homens. Davi conduzia o exército nas suas campanhas.
pt.R: Por isso Saul mandou Davi para longe da sua corte e o fez comandante de mil soldados. Davi liderava os soldados quando eles saíam para lutar e quando voltavam para casa.

am.L: ሳኦልም ከአጠገቡ አራቀው፤ ለራሱም የሺህ አለቃ አድርጎ ሾመው፤ በሕዝቡም ፊት ይወጣና ይገባ ነበር።
am.B: ስለዚህ ሳኦል ዳዊትን ከአጠገቡ አርቆ የሺህ ሰዎች አለቃ አደረገው። ዳዊትም ሠራዊቱን እየመራ ለጦርነት ይወጣና ይመለስ ነበር።
am.R: ስለዚህ ሳኦል ዳዊትን ከቤተ መንግሥቱ አርቆ የሺህ ወታደሮች አለቃ አደረገው። ዳዊትም ወታደሮቹ ለጦርነት ሲወጡና ወደ አገራቸው ሲመለሱ ይመራቸው ነበር።

decisions.choice: removed him from his presence: Saul sent David away from court
decisions.reason: Saul wants David out of his sight, but by sending him out to fight he gives him even more chances to succeed and to win the people's love (verses 14-16).

decisions.choice: commander of a thousand: the leader of one of the army's larger units
decisions.reason: A "thousand" was a unit of the army, whose actual size may have been smaller (8:12; 17:18; see the note at Numbers 1:21). David had already been set over the fighting men (verse 5); now he has a command of his own in the field.

decisions.choice: went out and came in before the people: led the army in its campaigns
decisions.reason: To "go out and come in before" people means to lead them in war (verse 16; Numbers 27:17; Joshua 14:11). "The people" here is the army, as often in Samuel.

decisions.choice: led the army in its campaigns (Balanced); led the soldiers when they went out to fight and when they came home (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable explain the idiom and say that "the people" are the army.

source.text: וַיְהִ֥י דָוִ֛ד לְכָל־דָּרְכָ֖ומַשְׂכִּ֑יל וַֽיהוָ֖ה עִמּֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: And was David in all his ways succeeding, and Yahweh [was] with him.

en.L: And David was succeeding in all his ways, and {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} [was] with him.
en.B: David succeeded in everything he did, for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} was with him.
en.R: David did well in everything he did, because {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} was with him.

es.L: Y David tenía éxito en todos sus caminos, y {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} [estaba] con él.
es.B: David tenía éxito en todo lo que hacía, pues {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} estaba con él.
es.R: A David le iba bien en todo lo que hacía, porque {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} estaba con él.

fr.L: Et David réussissait dans toutes ses voies, et {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} [était] avec lui.
fr.B: David réussissait dans tout ce qu’il entreprenait, car {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} était avec lui.
fr.R: David réussissait tout ce qu’il faisait, parce que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} était avec lui.

sw.L: Daudi alikuwa akifanikiwa katika njia zake zote, na {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} [alikuwa] pamoja naye.
sw.B: Daudi alifanikiwa katika kila jambo alilofanya, kwa maana {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alikuwa pamoja naye.
sw.R: Daudi alifanikiwa katika kila jambo alilofanya, kwa sababu {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alikuwa pamoja naye.

vi.L: Đa-vít thành công trong mọi đường lối mình, và {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} [ở] với ông.
vi.B: Đa-vít thành công trong mọi việc ông làm, vì {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} ở với ông.
vi.R: Đa-vít làm việc gì cũng tốt đẹp, vì {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} ở với ông.

ko.L: 그리고 다윗은 그의 모든 길에서 일을 잘 해냈고, {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 그와 함께 계셨다.
ko.B: 다윗은 하는 일마다 잘 해냈다. {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 그와 함께 계셨기 때문이다.
ko.R: 다윗은 무슨 일을 하든지 잘 해냈다. {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 그와 함께 계셨기 때문이다.

pt.L: E Davi era bem-sucedido em todos os seus caminhos, e {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} [estava] com ele.
pt.B: Davi se saía bem em tudo o que fazia, pois {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} estava com ele.
pt.R: Davi se saía bem em tudo o que fazia, porque {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} estava com ele.

am.L: ዳዊትም በመንገዱ ሁሉ ይከናወንለት ነበር፤ {{divine_name:እግዚአብሔር|ያህዌ}}ም ከእርሱ ጋር [ነበረ]።
am.B: {{divine_name:እግዚአብሔር|ያህዌ}} ከእርሱ ጋር ስለ ነበረ ዳዊት በሚያደርገው ነገር ሁሉ ይሳካለት ነበር።
am.R: {{divine_name:እግዚአብሔር|ያህዌ}} ከዳዊት ጋር ስለ ነበረ ያደረገው ነገር ሁሉ ተሳካለት።

decisions.choice: succeeding in all his ways: acting wisely and doing well in everything
decisions.reason: "Ways" means his undertakings. The verb is the one used in verse 5: David acts with good sense and succeeds.

decisions.choice: and Yahweh was with him: the reason for David's success
alternatives: and also Yahweh was with him
decisions.reason: The two clauses are joined by "and", but the second explains the first, as in verse 12 and 16:18.

decisions.choice: for / because
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable state the link that the Hebrew "and" implies.

source.text: וַיַּ֣רְא שָׁא֔וּל אֲשֶׁר־ה֖וּא מַשְׂכִּ֣יל מְאֹ֑ד וַיָּ֖גָר מִפָּנָֽיו׃

records.literal_gloss: And saw Saul that he [was] succeeding greatly, and he dreaded from before him.

en.L: And Saul saw that he was succeeding greatly, and he dreaded him.
en.B: When Saul saw how very successful David was, he was in dread of him.
en.R: Saul saw that David was doing very well, and that made Saul even more afraid of him.

es.L: Y vio Saúl que tenía mucho éxito, y le tuvo pavor.
es.B: Cuando Saúl vio lo mucho que prosperaba David, le tuvo pavor.
es.R: Saúl vio que a David le iba muy bien, y eso hizo que le tuviera todavía más miedo.

fr.L: Et Saül vit qu’il réussissait très bien, et il le redouta.
fr.B: Voyant que David réussissait si bien, Saül en eut une grande crainte.
fr.R: Saül a vu que David réussissait très bien, et il a eu encore plus peur de lui.

sw.L: Sauli akaona kwamba alikuwa akifanikiwa sana, akamhofu.
sw.B: Sauli alipoona jinsi Daudi alivyofanikiwa sana, akamhofu mno.
sw.R: Sauli akaona kwamba Daudi alikuwa akifanikiwa sana, na jambo hilo likamfanya amwogope hata zaidi.

vi.L: Sau-lơ thấy ông rất thành công thì khiếp sợ ông.
vi.B: Khi Sau-lơ thấy Đa-vít thành công rực rỡ như vậy, ông khiếp sợ Đa-vít.
vi.R: Sau-lơ thấy Đa-vít làm việc gì cũng thành công, và điều đó làm cho vua càng sợ ông hơn.

ko.L: 그리고 사울은 그가 크게 일을 잘 해내는 것을 보고 그를 두려워했다.
ko.B: 사울은 다윗이 하는 일마다 크게 잘되는 것을 보고 그를 몹시 두려워했다.
ko.R: 사울은 다윗이 무슨 일이든 아주 잘 해내는 것을 보았다. 그래서 다윗을 더욱 두려워하게 되었다.

pt.L: E Saul viu que ele era muito bem-sucedido, e teve pavor dele.
pt.B: Quando Saul viu como Davi era bem-sucedido, passou a ter pavor dele.
pt.R: Saul viu que Davi se saía muito bem, e isso fez Saul ter ainda mais medo dele.

am.L: ሳኦልም እጅግ እንደ ተከናወነለት አየ፤ ከፊቱም ፈራ።
am.B: ሳኦል ዳዊት እጅግ እንደ ተሳካለት ባየ ጊዜ በፍርሃት ተዋጠበት።
am.R: ሳኦል ዳዊት በጣም እንደ ተሳካለት አየ፤ ይህም ይበልጥ እንዲፈራው አደረገው።

decisions.choice: dreaded: was in fear and awe of him
decisions.reason: This verb is a stronger word for fear than the one in verse 12. It can mean to stand in awe or to shrink back in fear.

decisions.choice: even more afraid
decisions.reason: Readable shows that this fear goes beyond the fear of verse 12.

records.literal_gloss: And all Israel and Judah [were] loving David, because he [was] going out and coming in before them.

en.L: And all Israel and Judah loved David, because he was going out and coming in before them.
en.B: But all Israel and Judah loved David, because he led them in their campaigns.
en.R: But all the people of Israel and Judah loved David, because he was the one who led them into battle.

es.L: Pero todo Israel y Judá amaban a David, porque él salía y entraba delante de ellos.
es.B: Pero todo Israel y Judá amaban a David, porque él los dirigía en sus campañas.
es.R: Pero toda la gente de Israel y de Judá quería a David, porque él era quien los llevaba a la batalla.

fr.L: Et tout Israël et Juda aimaient David, car il sortait et rentrait devant eux.
fr.B: Mais tout Israël et Juda aimaient David, parce qu’il les conduisait dans leurs campagnes.
fr.R: Mais tout le peuple d’Israël et de Juda aimait David, parce que c’était lui qui les conduisait au combat.

sw.B: Lakini Israeli wote na Yuda walimpenda Daudi, kwa sababu ndiye aliyewaongoza katika vita vyao.
sw.R: Lakini watu wote wa Israeli na Yuda walimpenda Daudi, kwa sababu ndiye aliyewaongoza vitani.

vi.B: Nhưng cả Y-sơ-ra-ên và Giu-đa đều yêu mến Đa-vít, vì ông dẫn họ ra trận.
vi.R: Nhưng toàn dân Y-sơ-ra-ên và Giu-đa đều yêu mến Đa-vít, vì ông là người dẫn họ ra chiến trận.

ko.B: 그러나 온 이스라엘과 유다는 다윗을 사랑했다. 다윗이 그들을 이끌고 싸움터에 나가고 들어왔기 때문이다.
ko.R: 그러나 이스라엘과 유다의 모든 백성은 다윗을 사랑했다. 다윗이 앞장서서 그들을 이끌고 싸웠기 때문이다.
